accuracy.evidence: Checked against the DfE 2013 KS1 English programme of study for Year 2 writing composition (develop stamina by writing narratives about personal experiences, real events and for different purposes, plan or say aloud what they will write, re-read and check) and CCSS W.1.3, W.1.2 and W.2.2. Recounts are described as past tense in time order with time words; instructions as numbered steps led by bossy (imperative) verbs; a letter as greeting, message and sign-off. The adult text treats stamina as a habit built by short daily writing, not a test of length.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the Year 1–2 slips teachers report: writing a recount in the present or future tense (prediction and tag tense), putting instruction steps out of order (seed-pot step, tag order), mixing up which form suits a purpose (tag form), forgetting the parts of a letter (tag letter) and stopping at the first stuck moment instead of using a strategy such as saying the next sentence aloud (tag quit).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagstam builds four kinds of writing: choose a form for a purpose, order the steps that make a seed pot grow on screen, rewrite a recount into past tense with time words, lay out a letter, and keep a stamina page going through stuck moments. It shares no model with the phonics, sentence or story labs, and the 30 percent shingle gate passed against every flagship lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: The child sees each idea work before it is named: steps in the wrong order leave the pot empty, the right order makes the shoot pop up, a recount line changes colour when the tense becomes past, the letter only reads properly once greeting and sign-off are in place, and the stamina bar keeps filling after each stuck moment is solved with a strategy.

predictions.evidence: Four locked predictions with tempting wrong options: which kind of writing tells someone how to do a job, whether instruction order matters, which recount sentence is right (present and future tense options), and what to do when you get stuck (stop, or keep going with a strategy). A.reveal repeats the child's guess beside the result.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Rotating challenge on tense, order, form, letter parts and quitting; every wrong answer is tagged and why() gives a one-line reason in child words, for example a recount tells what already happened so it uses we went, not we go. Answers rotate so the right one is not always first.

readability.evidence: Family audience for ages 6–7: kid paragraphs are short read-aloud sentences under the family kid FK limit; the adult paragraphs were rewritten into short sentences and score about 5 on the FK check, using the Year 2 terms recount, instructions, imperative (bossy) verbs, time connectives and composition.

no_filler.evidence: Filler gate passed and overlap with every other lesson, including the story-writing and sentence lessons, is under 12 percent. Each kid paragraph adds one form or one stamina habit; the adult paragraphs give the curriculum links, named mistakes and how to build stamina at home.

mobile.evidence: Android 360 px and iPhone 13 screenshots in light and dark after every Show me. The instructions step was re-laid out (pot at the left, numbered list from 34 percent of the width) after the step text clipped at 360 px; the re-check shows all four steps and the shoot clear of the list. Young-class buttons are large and full width.

accessibility.evidence: walk.cjs passed: axe found no WCAG 2.1 AA violations in light or dark on desktop and iPhone 13, with no console errors, all Show me tasks completed and the challenge showed. Every canvas action has a large button twin, and the canvas aria-label speaks each result, such as which step comes next.

sources: DfE (2013) National curriculum in England: English programmes of study KS1, Year 2 Writing – composition
DfE (2013) English Appendix 2: Vocabulary, grammar and punctuation, Years 1–2 (tense, sentence types)
CCSS ELA W.1.3, W.1.2, W.2.2 (narrative and informative/explanatory writing)
EEF (2017) Improving Literacy in Key Stage 1, Recommendation 5: writing composition and transcription
